# DataRaft and the Modern Data Stack {#sec-modern-stack}

DataRaft is most useful when its role is described in terms of responsibilities rather than tool competition.

## DuckDB and DuckLake

DuckDB is an execution and storage engine. DataRaft can use it through the lake component and adapters. DuckLake adds catalog and data-lake semantics on top of DuckDB-oriented workflows. DataRaft contributes product definitions, quality gates, release evidence, and lifecycle behavior around those physical systems.

## dbt

The experimental `dataraft.dbt` package can describe a dbt project, run builds, inspect artifacts, import bounded contract information, and publish checked outputs through a configured DataRaft lake.

The integration does not claim that a normal dbt run is automatically an atomic DataRaft release. Managed publication is a separate step.

Use dbt as the primary transformation system when SQL models, warehouse-native workflows, and a cross-language analytics engineering team are the center of gravity. Use DataRaft when R-defined products and R-side checks, diagnostics, or publication evidence are important. The two can coexist.

## Pointblank

Pointblank is a specialized data validation engine. DataRaft can use it for checks while retaining its own product-level gate and evidence model.

## OpenMetadata and OpenLineage

OpenMetadata is an external metadata/catalog system. OpenLineage is a lineage event standard. DataRaft adapters can publish to both. Neither replaces the local executable definition.

## Semantic layers

`dataraft.metrics` is experimental and explicitly not a general semantic modeling engine. If the organization needs universal metrics across BI tools with join semantics, time grains, access policies, and SQL generation, use a purpose-built semantic layer and integrate it at the product boundary.

## Orchestration

DataRaft defines and executes product workflows, but it is not a general scheduler. Use GitHub Actions, Posit Connect, Airflow, Dagster, targets, or another orchestrator for recurring triggers when those capabilities are needed.

::: {.callout-note title="A useful test"}
If another tool already owns a concern well, ask whether DataRaft should integrate with it rather than reproduce it. Modularity is valuable only when the boundaries stay clear.
:::

## Integration by responsibility

It is easier to position DataRaft by asking which responsibility a tool owns.

| Responsibility | DataRaft role | Other common tools |
|---|---|---|
| product definition | core concept | contracts in dbt or platform catalogs |
| preparation | R recipes and transforms | dplyr, SQL, dbt |
| quality | native rules, optional Pointblank | Pointblank, dbt tests, warehouse checks |
| durable release history | DataRaft lake or adapters | lakehouse and warehouse systems |
| metadata export | adapters | OpenMetadata, OpenLineage |
| SQL project execution | optional dbt integration | dbt |
| metric evidence | experimental metrics package | semantic/metrics layers |
| scheduling | delegated | GitHub Actions, Posit Connect, orchestrators |

The table is not a scorecard. In a mature environment, several of these tools can be present at the same time.

### dbt

`dataraft.dbt` is explicitly experimental. It can describe and run dbt projects, inspect artifacts, derive bounded contract information from manifests, expose lineage, and publish checked outputs through a configured DataRaft lake. Running dbt by itself does not create an atomic DataRaft release.

Use the integration when SQL models already belong in dbt. Do not rewrite a successful dbt project into R merely to make DataRaft the center of every transformation.

### DuckDB and DuckLake

DuckDB is an execution and storage engine used by the lake implementation and some optional workflows. DuckLake adds a lake-oriented metadata/storage architecture. Neither is the DataRaft product model itself. This distinction keeps DataRaft from becoming synonymous with a single backend.

### Semantic layers and metrics

`dataraft.metrics` is experimental and deliberately states that it is not a general semantic modeling engine. It can define metrics, retain the exact checked release used for a measurement, store runtime evidence, and verify frozen report values. Joins, additivity, time-grain semantics, and general SQL semantic modeling remain with the product or an external semantic system.

### Orchestration

DataRaft has an execution graph, but it does not attempt to replace a full scheduler. Use an external scheduler when you need retries across machines, event triggers, queues, resource management, or organization-wide dependency scheduling. The DataRaft command invoked by that scheduler can still own the product-level acceptance gate.

## Exercises

1. For a stack containing dbt, DuckDB, OpenMetadata, and DataRaft, assign one primary responsibility to each component. Avoid giving the same responsibility to two tools.
2. Choose a workflow where dbt should be the primary modeling tool and explain what DataRaft could still add around checked releases.
3. Choose a workflow where DataRaft alone is enough and adding a catalog or orchestrator would be premature.
